extraction.segment_function: Analyzing the nature of power, strength, force, and their relationship to human plurality, organization, and tyranny.

claims.claim: Power is generated and kept alive solely by the living together of people in action and organization, and whoever isolates himself forfeits power.
claims.supporting_excerpt: The only indispensable material factor in the generation of power is the living together of people. Only where men live so close together that the potentialities of action are always present can power remain with them, and the foundation of cities, which as city-states have remained paradigmatic for all Western political organization, is therefore indeed the most important material prerequisite for power.

claims.claim: Tyranny rests fundamentally on isolation and contradicts human plurality, thereby generating impotence rather than power.
claims.supporting_excerpt: Montesquieu realized that the outstanding characteristic of tyranny was that it rested on isolation—on the isolation of the tyrant from his subjects and the isolation of the subjects from each other through mutual fear and suspicion—and hence that tyranny was not one form of government among others but contradicted the essential human condition of plurality

definitions.definition: The potentiality in being together, kept alive through organization and remaining together, corresponding to human plurality and boundless in nature.
An individual physical attribute that is indivisible, kept in bounds by plurality, and distinct from the power of collective action.
That which one man alone can exert against fellow men, associated with violence and the means of violence, which can destroy power but never substitute for it.

distinctions.distinction: Power depends on the agreement of many wills in being together and is boundless and divisible, whereas strength is an individual physical characteristic that is indivisible and bounded by the presence of others.
Power is generated by people living together in plurality, whereas force can be exerted by a single individual or few through violence and can destroy power but never substitute for it.

must_not_be_lost: The distinction between power, strength, and force.
Montesquieu's insight that tyranny rests on isolation and contradicts human plurality.
